questions: Does y=0.03 m change max_error or steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom compared with y=0.05 m (iteration 4)?
Does line_loss_events rise at y=0.03 m, and on which track and bend does it occur?
Does progress move with the shorter lead, or is it still fixed by the off-track end regardless of sensor position?
Is control_effort lower or higher than iteration 4 on the s-bend, which would show whether the controller is working harder with less lead?

intent: Test whether a shorter sensor lead (y=0.03 m, down from 0.05 m) reduces the overshoot and lag that pin max_error at the 0.06 m floor. Everything else matches iteration 4, the best design so far (58.54), so the race isolates the forward-position change. The sensor span (+/-0.06 m, 7 sensors, 16 mm) is kept because it removed most line loss. I expect progress to hold near 0.18 on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error and steering_oscillation at or below iteration 4 levels.
learning: Iterations 5 to 7 bracketed wheel_radius: 0.025 m gave 57.9 and 0.04 m gave 41.4, so 0.03 m is near optimal. Mass 1.0 kg hurt (42.7), so 0.8 kg stays. The sensor-lead direction has only been tested upward (y=0.07, confounded with body and mass changes, and it hurt). This iteration tests the downward direction alone. If y=0.03 helps, the next step is an even shorter lead or sensor_size 0.012. If it hurts, y=0.05 is the optimum and the remaining geometry levers are body_length alone (inertia, untested in isolation) and sensor_size.
rationale: Evidence across iterations 0 to 7: every run ends off_track on all three development tracks, and max_error sits on the 0.06 m off-track floor. The floor is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 m for every allowed body width, so body width cannot help. Line loss is now rare (oval 0, s-bend about 0.95, slalom about 0.85 at iteration 4), so sensor span is no longer the limit. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.08, wheel_radius 0.03, mass 0.8, 7 sensors at y=0.05, 16 mm footprints, body 0.18 x 0.12) remains the best at 58.54. Iteration 7 (wheel_radius 0.025) scored 57.92, slightly lower, so radius 0.03 is near the optimum. Radius 0.04 (iteration 5) and mass 1.0 (iteration 6) both cut s-bend progress sharply. Iteration 2 moved the sensors forward to y=0.07 together with a shorter, lighter body, and that hurt. The sensor-lead direction was therefore confounded and never tested alone in the shorter direction. I now revert to iteration 4 and change only the forward sensor position, from y=0.05 to y=0.03 m. The hypothesis is that a shorter lead reduces the overshoot that builds when the controller responds to line position well ahead of the wheels on bends. I expect s-bend and slalom progress to hold near 0.18 or rise, with max_error still at or near the floor. Risk: a shorter lead may increase lag and push line loss up on the sharpest bends.
